title: Intel, from Lunar Lake to Razer Lake
gist: Short SemiWiki forum thread on Intel's client roadmap from Lunar Lake to Razer Lake: posters note that on-package memory for the high-end Razer Lake-AX is sourced by OEMs rather than Intel (avoiding Lunar Lake's DRAM-cost margin hit), and that the AX part uses a 256-bit, 4-chip LPDDR bus while 128-bit U/H variants need only 2 chips.

insights.claim: On Intel's Razer Lake-AX packages, the on-package memory is the responsibility of OEMs/vendors rather than Intel, shielding Intel from the Lunar Lake situation where RAM cost hurt its margins.
insights.speaker: siliconbruh999
insights.so_what: Removes a memory-price pass-through risk from Intel client gross margins versus the Lunar Lake generation; watch DRAM pricing impact on Intel client margins.
insights.quote: the Memory on RZL-AX Packages is the responsibility of OEM/Vendors not Intel so they are going to be saved from LNL Situation of the RAM Cost affecting margins
insights.locator: there is a one interesting thing about RZL-AX

insights.claim: A forum moderator hopes Intel will support low-DRAM client products as an option, reflecting concern about memory cost/configuration in on-package designs.
insights.speaker: MKWVentures
insights.so_what: Signals buyer/OEM sensitivity to DRAM content and cost in client SKUs.
insights.quote: I hope Intel supports low dram products as an option.
insights.locator: is there a full client roadmap available online

themes.theme: Razer Lake bus widths and segmentation

insights.claim: The Razer Lake package shown appears to be the high-end 'AMD Halo' competitor variant with a 256-bit memory bus using 4 LPDDR chips.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Intel is targeting AMD's Halo-class large-iGPU/unified-memory segment with an on-package wide-bus part.
insights.quote: The package above appears to be the higher end "AMD Halo" competitor version of Razor Lake with a 256-bit bus (4 chips).

insights.claim: Intel's mainstream Razer Lake-U and Razer Lake-H variants are expected to use a 128-bit bus needing only 2 memory chips, implying a likely 16GB base memory configuration.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Lower memory content per mainstream laptop affects DRAM demand per unit.
insights.locator: There should be 128-bit versions as well

insights.claim: Intel's Wildcat Lake, a cut-down Panther Lake, has a 64-bit-wide memory bus, and it is unclear whether on-package-memory versions of its refresh or successors will come.
insights.speaker: Xebec
insights.so_what: Defines the low end of Intel's client memory-width ladder.
